findings.reason: the node should first confirm the existing guard still loses the race under load (the plan asserts a product lost-update) and otherwise add the missing test, not fork the mechanism.
findings.text: §13 designs a publish-time check that the pointer "still exists and the run is not discarded" with no reference to `_write_existing_pointer` (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:5030), which already performs that two-sided existence check and was committed for this exact race in 3120843f6 today, so the section risks reimplementing a guard that is already in the tree

findings.reason: §12 should reuse the existing event-wait helper rather than introduce a second bounding approach for the same file.
findings.text: §12 asks the case to "wait on the event it asserts rather than a wall-clock window, or bound its window from a measured figure" without citing the event-wait helper and measured bound the §14 node already built (`_wait_for` at tests/test_dispatch_returns_without_worker.py:705 and `_dispatch_exit_bound`/`_survival_window_seconds` at :825-842)

findings.reason: the hold-or-divert behaviour should extend the existing verdict (e.g. wait-then-release or divert-with-report inside it) instead of adding a parallel member-busy decision that can drift from `node.py`.
findings.text: §11 routes a launch onto a busy member through a dispatch-side "hold or divert" path without saying why the guard that already decides member busyness, `member_in_flight_verdict` / `refuse_member_in_flight` (reckon/crew/node.py:357,391), cannot be extended; the plan's own code comment binds that semantic to the same guard (dispatch.py:11365)

findings.reason: the owner is recovery.py's classification arm; the plan should extend it (or, if the observed collision kills the process before `launch_failures` is written, prove that residual case and cite the gap) rather than add a second stderr reader.
findings.text: §11's clause to make `observe` read `stderr.log` when the stream is empty so a launch failure classifies `launch-failed` with its reason attached duplicates the existing launch-failed arm in recovery.py:8697-8738, which already reads `latest["stderr_tail"]` captured by dispatch.py:7963 and names the cause

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the per-run supervisor hides the snapshot, the spawn, the wait and the exit record behind one entry point (`_start_supervisor` reaching `reckon/crew/supervisor_main.py`), and the live §12–§14 add tests and a dispatch-side guard over existing helpers rather than new modules; no shallow-wrapper sprawl is introduced.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §11's clause to make `observe` read `stderr.log` so a launch failure classifies `launch-failed` with its reason duplicates the launch-failed reader in `reckon/crew/recovery.py:8697-8738`, which already surfaces the stderr tail `dispatch.py:7963` captures; the owner to extend is `recovery.py`.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the live design sections (§12, §13) propose repairs without citing mechanisms that already exist for their exact defect: `_write_existing_pointer` (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:5030) for the discard-vs-publish race, and the `_wait_for`/`_dispatch_exit_bound` event-wait the §14 case built (tests/test_dispatch_returns_without_worker.py:825-854).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §11 adds a hold-or-divert path for a busy member with no statement why the existing member guard cannot be extended, so a second member-busy decision lands beside the one `refuse_member_in_flight` already makes.
